t: This is the General Post Office on Newgate Street, in the City of London. It was designed by two architects who both worked for His Majesty's Office of Works. Henry Tanner was a prominent British architect of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Richard Allison, a Scottish architect, was associated with the Office of Works from 1889 and became its chief architect in 1914. It is very much a government building, shaped by the officials who designed the nation's public premises.
